q: Oxygen is the most abundant element in the Earth’s crust. The free element accounts for ____ of the volume of the atmosphere.
e: This percentage indicates the proportion of oxygen in the atmosphere, essential for respiration.

q: Oxygen in the combined state exists in water, sand or silica, silicates and ____ .
e: Rocks are natural solid aggregates of minerals and can contain oxygen in various forms.

q: Oxygen preparation can be demonstrated in a number of ways in the classroom or in the ____ .
e: The laboratory setting allows for controlled experiments to demonstrate chemical reactions.

q: Potassium chlorate should not be used for the preparation of oxygen in the laboratory due to its ____ nature.
e: Toxic substances can pose health risks if inhaled or ingested.

q: In the laboratory or in the classroom, oxygen gas can be prepared by using an environmentally friendly liquid ____ of appropriate strength.
e: Hydrogen peroxide is a common reagent used to generate oxygen gas safely.

q: In this reaction, manganese(IV) oxide is used as a ____ to speed up the chemical reaction.
e: A catalyst increases the rate of a chemical reaction without being consumed in the process.

q: Oxygen gas is collected by the downward displacement of ____ .
e: This method utilizes the property of gases being less dense than liquids to collect gas.

q: Oxygen is a colourless gas, without taste or smell. Oxygen is only slightly soluble in ____ .
e: Solubility in water affects how oxygen is available for aquatic life.

q: Oxygen will not burn; however, it supports ____ .
e: Combustion is the chemical process of burning that requires oxygen.

q: If rekindles any glowing thing (splinter) with a bright flame, it indicates the presence of ____ .
e: The rekindling of a splinter shows that oxygen supports combustion.

q: Metals such as magnesium, iron, copper and zinc react with oxygen forming ____ .
e: Oxides are compounds formed when elements react with oxygen.

q: A piece of clean magnesium ribbon continues burning in oxygen from air with a dazzling white flame, leaving a white powder as ____ .
e: Residue is the solid left after a reaction, in this case, magnesium oxide.

q: This residue is magnesium oxide: magnesium + oxygen -> ____ .
e: Magnesium oxide is the product of the reaction between magnesium and oxygen.

q: Iron slowly becomes oxidised in the presence of air and water, to form hydrated iron(II) oxide, i.e., iron has become ____ .
e: Rusting is the corrosion of iron caused by oxidation.

q: Most useful metals or sheets become covered with thin films of metal ____ .
e: Metal oxides can protect metals from further corrosion.

q: Non-metals such as phosphorus, sulphur and carbon react with oxygen to form ____ .
e: Non-metal oxides are products of reactions between non-metals and oxygen.

q: A small piece of phosphorus burns in oxygen giving off white fumes which consist of oxides of ____ .
e: Phosphorus oxides are formed when phosphorus reacts with oxygen.

q: Phosphorus + oxygen -> ____ .
e: Phosphorus(V) oxide is formed in this reaction.

q: Phosphorus + oxygen -> ____ .
e: Phosphorus(III) oxide is another product of phosphorus reacting with oxygen.

q: An oxide is a compound containing ____ and another element.
e: Oxygen is a key element in oxides, which can form with various other elements.

q: An acidic oxide is an oxide of ____ .
e: Acidic oxides typically come from non-metallic elements.

q: Acidic oxides react with basic oxides to give ____ only.
e: Salts are the products of neutralization reactions between acids and bases.

q: Some acidic oxides are soluble in water but some are not. CO2, SO2, SO3 and P2O5 are soluble oxides while SiO2 is an ____ oxide.
e: Insoluble oxides do not dissolve in water to form acidic solutions.

q: Soluble acidic oxides dissolve in water to form acidic solutions. These solutions turn blue litmus ____ .
e: Litmus paper changes color in response to acidity.

q: Sulphur trioxide + water -> ____ .
e: Sulphuric acid is formed from the reaction of sulphur trioxide with water.

q: A basic oxide is an oxide of ____ .
e: Basic oxides are derived from metallic elements.

q: A basic oxide reacts with an acid to produce a ____ and water only.
e: The reaction between an acid and a base produces salt and water.

q: A basic oxide neutralises ____ .
e: Basic oxides react with acids to form salts.

q: Some basic oxides are soluble in water but some are not. Na2O and K2O are soluble oxides while MgO, CuO and Ag2O are ____ .
e: These oxides do not dissolve in water to form alkaline solutions.

q: Some basic oxides react with water forming ____ solutions (alkalis).
e: Hydroxide solutions are alkaline and turn red litmus blue.

q: Sodium oxide + water -> ____ .
e: Sodium hydroxide is formed when sodium oxide reacts with water.

q: An amphoteric oxide is a metallic oxide which possesses both, basic and ____ properties.
e: Amphoteric oxides can react with both acids and bases.

q: An amphoteric oxide reacts with both acids and alkalis to form ____ and water.
e: The reaction with acids and bases produces salt and water.

q: Zinc oxide + sulphuric acid (dil.) -> ____ .
e: Zinc sulphate is formed from the reaction of zinc oxide with sulphuric acid.

q: Zinc oxide + sodium hydroxide -> ____ .
e: Sodium zincate is produced when zinc oxide reacts with sodium hydroxide.

q: The neutral oxide is an oxide which shows neither basic nor ____ character.
e: Neutral oxides do not exhibit the properties of acids or bases.

q: Those oxides that react with an acid to give salt and hydrogen peroxide are called ____ .
e: Peroxides release hydrogen peroxide when reacting with acids.

q: A compound oxide is an oxide, formed by the combination of two different oxides of the same ____ .
e: Compound oxides consist of two oxides of the same element.

q: PbO2 is a compound oxide consisting of lead(II) and lead(IV) oxides. It can be written as di-lead(II) lead(IV) oxide or ____ lead oxide.
e: Red lead oxide is a well-known compound oxide.

q: When red lead oxide reacts with dilute nitric acid, lead(II) oxide only reacts with the acid to form lead(II) ____ .
e: Lead(II) nitrate is produced from the reaction with nitric acid.

q: Oxygen is used to help patients with ____ difficulties.
e: Breathing difficulties can be alleviated with supplemental oxygen.

q: In aquatic habitat, organisms use oxygen dissolved in ____ .
e: Aquatic organisms rely on dissolved oxygen for respiration.

q: In living organisms, the oxygen intake is used for the breakdown of the glucose molecules to produce ____ .
e: Energy is produced through cellular respiration using oxygen.

q: Oxygen is used in steel work, and oxyacetylene gas mixture is used for ____ and welding metals.
e: Cutting metals requires high temperatures generated by oxyacetylene flames.

q: Liquid oxygen is carried on rockets to support the fuel ____ .
e: Liquid oxygen is essential for combustion in rocket engines.

q: Usefulness of some oxides in society includes their role as bleaching agents, pigments used in paints, and in cement ____ .
e: Oxides play various roles in industrial applications.
